field_id_lesson.look_here_first: Do not identify this grass from a general bluestem silhouette. Start with the subtending leafy spathe, then examine the paired racemes and sessile versus pedicellate spikelets. Photograph a mature unit with a millimeter scale; compare the same structures against other Anatherum cards before naming it.
crew_checkpoints: Document the entire flowering culm and where each raceme pair emerges from its spathe.
Measure the spathe and raceme length from a mature specimen; retain actual measurements rather than guessing species-level thresholds.
At 10–20× magnification photograph the rachis joints, paired spikelets, awn insertion and visible hairs with a millimeter reference.
Photograph the leaf collar and ligule, then compare the complete reproductive unit against source-verified specimens.

look_alikes.check: Bushy bluestem has a conspicuously dense brushlike crown of many crowded silky short racemes; do not equate one fluffy pair with the whole crown.
Broomsedge typically shows more individually separated spathe-enclosed flowering units; confirm by spathe and spikelet detail.
Little bluestem produces silky racemes on separate branches; compare branch placement and spikelet structure.
